paras: The killing of Erasmus Coffman was the fatal shooting of a Black convict laborer by a guard on a Valley Railroad construction contract near Staunton, Virginia, about 19 April 1882. According to the Staunton papers, Coffman was shot while attempting to escape and was killed. The shooting was reported in brief local items and in one Washington news column.

Coffman, described as "colored," was a convict leased to the contractors Gooch & Mason, whose names some items printed as Mason & Gooch, on the Valley Railroad. The work was about four miles south of Staunton.

On a Wednesday in the week before 25 April, Coffman tried to escape from the convict force. The Staunton Spectator reported that the guard shot him twice and killed him. The Staunton Vindicator said instead that he was "fired on by the guard and so severely wounded that he died." Neither paper named the guard or described the escape attempt beyond those words.
No report of an inquest, an arrest of the guard, or any investigation appears in the coverage.

Both Staunton papers treated the shooting as a short local item, headed "CONVICT KILLED" in the Spectator on 25 April and "CONVICT SHOT" in the Vindicator on 28 April. Each gave the escape attempt as the reason for the shooting and added no comment. The Spectator ran a second, similar item, "A CONVICT KILLED," on 2 May.
On 29 April the Washington National Republican included the story, credited to the Spectator, among its "Virginia News" briefs, between notes on a railroad official's move and a horse theft.

reader.title: Killing of Erasmus Coffman
bases: A guard over contract convicts shot Coffman while he was trying to escape custody; no mob or crowd is reported (A2, A3, A4).
Two Staunton papers, the Spectator and the Vindicator, independently report the shooting and death in their own wording (A2, A3); the Washington paper credits the Spectator (A4).
